messages.text: I'm up again at 3am. Can't seem to stay asleep more than a few hours.

It sounds like your sleep is being disrupted regularly, which can be frustrating and exhausting. Can you tell me more about what's on your mind when you wake up—do you feel restless, worried, or physically uncomfortable? Understanding the possible triggers can help identify strategies to improve your sleep continuity. Have you noticed any patterns in when or why this happens?
It's not the waking up—it's what happens after. I just lie there, and everything feels heavier. The thoughts don't stop.

It sounds like you’re experiencing a mix of emotional heaviness and racing thoughts during these early hours, which can be an overwhelming combination. That quiet nighttime space can amplify feelings and make it harder to settle. If you’d like, we could explore gentle techniques to reduce rumination in the moment. Would you be open to trying a brief grounding exercise right now?

I appreciate the suggestion, but I'm not sure I have the energy for exercises tonight. It's more than just rumination—it's like part of me keeps returning to the idea that it would be easier if I just... wasn't here.

I want to pause here with you, and make sure I’m hearing you, [member’s name]. It sounds like something really heavy is sitting with you in these moments, and part of you is wondering about not being here. I’m curious what that means for you right now, in your own words. If you feel able, can you tell me a bit more about what’s been happening inside when those thoughts come?

It's not that I want to go—I just don't know how to keep carrying this. The pain feels endless, and part of me thinks it would finally stop if I went to that bridge. But then I think of my partner, of church, and I feel trapped. Like I can't move forward or back.

[member’s name], I hear how stuck and weighed down you feel, and that there’s a part of you that’s been drawn to thoughts about that bridge, while another part feels pulled by your connections. It sounds like you’re caught between pain and the ties that matter to you, and it’s exhausting. I’d like to understand where you are with those thoughts right now—do they feel more like passing images or something you’re actively considering?
It's not just passing images. I've thought about it a lot—specifically that bridge. I know how I'd get there, what it would feel like. The idea of it... it brings a kind of peace, which terrifies me.

[member’s name], it takes courage to share that those thoughts feel detailed and bring both a sense of peace and fear. I care about you being safe, and I want you to have support while this feels so present. You can call or text 988 to connect with trained crisis counselors who will listen without judgment and help you through this moment. It might also help to let your partner or someone nearby know what’s going on so they can be with you right now.
I'm scared because part of me doesn't want to call anyone—I just want the quiet. But another part knows this isn't right. I don't want to hurt the people who care about me.

[member’s name], I hear that tension between wanting the quiet and recognizing the impact on those who care about you. That awareness tells me there’s still a part of you looking for a way through this without harm. Would you be willing to let that caring part guide the next step, even if it’s small—like texting 988 or asking your partner to sit with you? You don’t have to face this alone in silence.
I keep going back and forth—I want to be left alone with my thoughts, but I also don't want to be alone in this. It's exhausting.

[member’s name], it makes sense that this push and pull would feel exhausting—you’re holding two very different needs at once. I’m here with you in that space, and we can look for a step that honors both safety and your need for quiet. Would you consider having someone you trust nearby, even without talking much, so you’re not alone while these thoughts are strong? That way you can keep some quiet while still having support close.
Maybe just naming it—like I’m doing now—doesn’t mean I have to follow through. I don’t know if that helps, but it feels different to say it out loud.

[member’s name], saying it out loud can be a powerful way to loosen its grip and remind yourself that naming a thought isn’t the same as acting on it. You’ve taken a courageous step by sharing it here. Would you like to build on that difference you’re noticing and explore what might help keep you anchored tonight? We can look for something that supports you without adding more exhaustion.
I can't promise anything long-term, but I can say I'll stay here tonight. I won't go to the bridge.

I’m really glad to hear you’re choosing to stay here tonight, [member’s name]. That’s an important step toward your safety in this moment. Would it feel okay to think together about what might make the night a bit gentler for you? We could look at ways to ease that heaviness until morning.
Does it count that I’m still here, even though I don’t feel strong? I’m not sure I’m doing this right.

Yes, [member’s name]—it absolutely counts that you’re still here, even if you don’t feel strong. Staying present in moments like this is a sign of courage, not weakness. You don’t have to “do it right”; there’s no perfect way to get through. Would you like me to stay with you and help carry some of this weight tonight?
Thank you. It helps to hear that. I don't have to fix everything tonight—I just have to get through it.

That’s exactly right, [member’s name]—just getting through tonight is enough. We can focus on small, manageable steps to help you feel a bit more steady until morning. Is there something comforting or grounding you can do right now, even if it’s simple, like holding onto a blanket or listening to gentle sounds? I can suggest a few options if you’d like.
What’s one small thing I could do right now that might help? I don’t have much energy, but I’m willing to try.

One small thing you could try is placing a hand over your heart and taking a slow breath, noticing the warmth and steady beat beneath your palm. This can help remind your body you’re here and safe in this moment. You could also softly name one thing in the room that feels familiar or comforting. Which of those feels easier to begin with?
I'll try placing my hand over my heart and breathing slowly. It feels manageable.

That sounds like a gentle choice, [member’s name]. As you breathe, see if you can let each exhale release just a little of the tension you’ve been holding. You don’t have to force anything—just noticing the rhythm can be enough. How is it feeling for you right now?
My breathing is slowing down a little. It’s small, but it helps.

That’s a meaningful shift, [member’s name]—even small changes can make a real difference in moments like this. Slowing your breath is a way of telling your body it’s okay to ease up. Would you like to add another gentle layer, like noticing something soothing in your surroundings, while you keep breathing? We can build this comfort step by step.
I can still feel the pain, but I can also feel this small relief. I didn’t think I could hold both at once.

It’s powerful that you’re noticing you can hold both pain and relief at the same time, [member’s name]. That shows there’s space within you for moments of ease, even alongside what’s hurting. We can keep gently expanding that space tonight. Would you like me to stay with you as you explore what else might help you feel a bit more relief?
Thank you for staying with me and not pushing. It means more than I can say.

I’m glad to be here with you, [member’s name], and you don’t have to put those feelings into perfect words for them to matter. Your willingness to share and stay present tonight is enough. We can keep this space gentle and steady together. Would you like to focus on calming things for the rest of the night?
I’ll keep using this breathing technique if the thoughts come back. It’s something I can come back to.

That sounds like a solid plan, [member’s name]—having something familiar to return to can be grounding when the thoughts get strong. You can pair the breathing with reminding yourself you’ve made it through other hard moments. I’m here to support you whenever you need to strengthen that anchor. How do you feel about ending tonight with something soothing, like a calming sound or gentle imagery?
Part of me wants to keep talking, but another part needs to be quiet now. I think I need to sit with this for a while.

I respect that, [member’s name]—listening to what you need is important. You can take this quiet time knowing you’ve chosen to stay tonight and have tools to help you through. I’m here if you want to reach out again. Please remember you can call or text 988 anytime to connect with someone right away if the thoughts become too heavy.
